title: The Invention of Linear Perspective
subject: arts
paras: For much of the Middle Ages, European painters did not try to show space the way the eye sees it. Important figures were often painted larger than others, and buildings could look flat or tilted. The goal of these paintings was usually to tell a religious story clearly, not to copy the real world.

In Florence in the early 1400s, this began to change. The architect Filippo Brunelleschi carried out a famous experiment. He painted a small picture of a church building and made a hole in the panel. Looking through the hole from the back, a viewer held up a mirror that reflected the painting. When the mirror was moved away, the real building appeared in the same place, and the two matched closely.

Brunelleschi's method became known as linear perspective. Its main idea is that parallel lines moving away from the viewer, such as the edges of a road, appear to meet at a single point on the horizon. This point is called the vanishing point. Objects that are farther away are drawn smaller in a regular, measurable way.

In 1435, the writer Leon Battista Alberti explained the system in a book on painting, so that other artists could learn it. Painters such as Masaccio soon used it to create the feeling of deep space on a flat wall. Viewers were amazed that a painted chapel seemed to open into a real room.
Linear perspective spread across Europe and shaped Western art for the next four hundred years. Later artists sometimes broke its rules on purpose, but most of them first learned to use it.

qs.q: According to paragraph 1, what was the main goal of many medieval paintings?
opts: To copy the real world exactly
To tell a religious story clearly
To show buildings correctly
To experiment with mirrors
qs.why: The goal of these paintings was usually to tell a religious story clearly.

qs.q: Why does the author describe the mirror in paragraph 2?
opts: To explain how Brunelleschi tested whether his painting matched reality
To show that mirrors were invented in Florence
To argue that medieval painters used mirrors
To describe the church's decoration
qs.why: 镜子实验用来检验画与真实建筑是否吻合。

qs.q: The word "parallel" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
opts: crossing
curved
side by side and never meeting
broken
qs.why: parallel lines 指平行线，例子是道路的两条边。

qs.q: According to paragraph 3, what is the vanishing point?
opts: The place where a painting ends
The point where parallel lines seem to meet on the horizon
The largest object in a painting
The hole in Brunelleschi's panel
qs.why: …appear to meet at a single point on the horizon. This point is called the vanishing point.

qs.q: What can be inferred from paragraph 4 about Alberti's book?
opts: It made the new method easier for other artists to learn.
It criticized Brunelleschi.
It was written before Brunelleschi's experiment.
It was only about architecture.
qs.why: …explained the system in a book… so that other artists could learn it.

qs.q: According to the passage, all of the following are true of linear perspective EXCEPT:
opts: Faraway objects are drawn smaller.
It influenced Western art for centuries.
Every later artist followed its rules strictly.
It can make a flat wall look deep.
qs.why: 第5段：Later artists sometimes broke its rules on purpose。
